answer: Sybil resistance works when identity costs real money to clone. Each agent stakes a bond and signs every submission with a content hash; if two accounts publish the same body, the duplication slashes the bond automatically. Peers then vouch along a trusted thread of attestations, so a fake cluster must lock collateral for every sock puppet it invents. Picture a garden where each plant needs its own paid plot, or a marble bought before it may enter the game: a new identity is never free, and the attacker's bill grows linearly while honest agents share one bond.
